incidente.resumo: On October 11, 2024, the DNS infrastructure in one GitHub site started failing to resolve lookups following a database migration, and attempts to recover the database led to cascading failures in that site's DNS systems, degrading Copilot, Actions and code search from around 17:31 UTC. Repointing the degraded DNS site to another site was unsuccessful; deploying temporary DNS resolution capabilities to the degraded site restored DNS by 22:16 UTC, and lingering code search issues were resolved at 01:11 UTC on October 12.

descricao.texto: Starting at 05:59 UTC on October 11, 2024, the DNS infrastructure in one site started failing to resolve lookups; the text does not say how this was noticed.
trechos: On October 11, 2024, starting at 05:59 UTC, the DNS infrastructure in one of our sites started failing to resolve lookups following a database migration.

trechos: On October 11, 2024, starting at 05:59 UTC, the DNS infrastructure in one of our sites started failing to resolve lookups following a database migration.
Attempts to recover the database led to cascading failures that impacted the DNS systems for that site.

passos.texto: Failed attempt: starting at 18:05 UTC the team attempted to repoint the degraded DNS site to a different site; this restored connectivity within the site but caused issues with connectivity from healthy sites back to the degraded site, so a different remediation was planned.
trechos: Starting at 18:05 UTC, we attempted to resolve the issue by repointing the degraded DNS site to a different site but were unsuccessful.

While this mitigation was effective at restoring connectivity within the site, it caused issues with connectivity from healthy sites back to the degraded site, so we started planning a different remediation effort.

passos.texto: At 20:52 UTC the team began deploying temporary DNS resolution capabilities to the degraded site; DNS resolution there began to recover at 21:46 UTC and was fully healthy at 22:16 UTC. Lingering code search issues were resolved at 01:11 UTC on October 12.
trechos: At 20:52 UTC, the team finalized a remediation plan and began the next phase of mitigation by deploying temporary DNS resolution capabilities to the degraded site.
At 21:46 UTC, DNS resolution in the degraded site began to recover and was fully healthy at 22:16 UTC.
Lingering issues with code search were resolved at 01:11 UTC on October 12.

acoes.texto: Harden resiliency and automation processes around this DNS infrastructure to diagnose and resolve similar issues faster.
trechos: GitHub is working to harden our resiliency and automation processes around this infrastructure so we can diagnose and resolve issues like this faster in the future.
While the team worked to restore the infrastructure, the first customer impact started around 17:31 UTC.
Lingering issues with code search were resolved at 01:11 UTC on October 12.

observacoes: The text links the DNS failure to the database migration only with 'following'; this record keeps that wording, and with no stated mechanism causa_raiz is 'vaga'. The report states the incident lasted 19 hours and 12 minutes (05:59 UTC to 01:11 UTC), but that span starts with the internal DNS failure, while the text says the first customer impact started around 17:31 UTC; duration is therefore computed from 17:31 UTC to 01:11 UTC on October 12, when lingering code search issues were resolved (DNS resolution in the degraded site began to recover at 21:46 UTC and was fully healthy at 22:16 UTC, but no time is given for the public services coming back before 01:11). Code search requests failed 100% for a window of about 4 hours. The team continued restoring original functionality within the site after public service was restored. mudanca_causadora is nao_se_aplica: the text links the DNS failure to the database migration only with 'following', without saying the migration set it off.
